fixed.member: UI CSS position: absolute, position: fixed
fixed.summary: A document's absolutely positioned element is now placed against its nearest positioned ancestor (or a `<stack>`), else the document's outermost box, as CSS does (CSS Position 3 §2.1); it used to be placed in its parent's box whether or not the parent was positioned. A fixed element under a transformed ancestor, one whose `will-change` names a transform or filter, or one with `contain: layout` or `paint` is placed against that ancestor's box (CSS Transforms 1 §3, CSS Containment 2 §3.2), not the viewport. Give the intended parent `position: relative` where an absolute child relied on the old placement.
